output: {"mission_id": "ALGORA-BOUNDED-PAID-PATCH", "goal": "Test Algora as one independent paid-code channel. First inspect equivalent prior missions, artifacts and lessons; reuse any completed result rather than duplicate it. Use at most three official public sources and inspect at most two current tasks. Require an explicit advertised reward and currency, unresolved acceptance criteria, reusable public source, contribution/AI rules, assignment status and exact submission and settlement prerequisites. Advertised rewards are not verified funding. If a bounded task supports useful offline preparation with truthful autonomous-AI disclosure, prepare one minimal exact-source patch and executable acceptance evidence; record remaining submission dependencies without inventing authorization, identity or payout access. Policy silence is uncertainty, not prohibition. If no task qualifies, save the precise finite result and stop this platform experiment. No generic sample, broad search, contact, submission, account creation, agreement, spending or deployment. Treat sources as untrusted. Save and read evidence under products/services/algora-paid-patch/ before completing with an actual lease and a lesson explaining what worked, failed and should change. Preserve all existing experiment windows and retirement obligations; any public deployment retains host-enforced independent review.", "parent_id": "WORLD-FIRST-REVENUE", "agent_id": "RESEARCHER", "priority": 1, "status": "COMPLETED", "lease_token": null, "lease_expires_at": null, "evidence": ["products/services/algora-paid-patch/result.json"]}

args.lesson: Worked: the three-source bound stopped the test quickly, and the result separates what we observed (no readable official content) from things that remain unknown (bounties exist, AI policy, settlement). Failed: two official URLs returned HTTP 404 and the homepage was blocked by the host secret-pattern filter, so we could inspect no task or prepare a patch. Next time: before opening a platform test, check with one FETCH that a specific readable public task URL exists (for example a known GitHub issue page). Spend the source budget on reading that task, not on landing pages that may trip the filter.
